construct: Skeletal-muscle glycogen phosphorylase deficiency prevents phosphorolytic release of glucose-1-phosphate from muscle glycogen during exercise, causing exercise intolerance and the characteristic second-wind phenomenon.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Exercise-induced cramps early in exertion plus a second-wind phenomenon and biallelic PYGM variants identify McArdle disease. PYGM encodes skeletal-muscle glycogen phosphorylase, which releases glucose-1-phosphate from glycogen.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Pompe, debranching-enzyme, and branching-enzyme defects involve different enzymes and phenotypes; hepatic glycogen phosphorylase is a different isoenzyme and cannot explain the skeletal-muscle PYGM genotype.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The direct gene result eliminates an otherwise broader metabolic-myopathy differential; the queried reaction is exactly the enzymatic step catalyzed by muscle glycogen phosphorylase.
